review_scope: Read-only algebra, phase, scratch ownership, existing native receipt, and conditional score accounting; no native rerun or full-decoder verification by reviewer.
findings: The selected child-norm coordinate is XORed with the exact polynomial norm of its still-live parent, so it becomes zero coherently; no new measurement or phase is introduced by that toggle.
The original parent register is mapped to its GF64 quadratic tower only during the norm toggle and is restored to polynomial coordinates before use by source phase_product.
The borrowed bits enter the consuming 12-bit multiplication target at zero, and each subsequent SWAP/HMR leaves all target bits zero. They are not read as child_norm while borrowed.

Each source HMR mask is paid using the surviving original norm and the updated source half. This uses new_half times original_norm equals old_half, including zero by inv0 and irreducible-norm zero iff source zero.
Borrowed child bits are restored after the second consuming HMR and before the original parent norm is measured or reconstructed through child_norm.
Only independently allocated temporary qubits are freed; caller-owned child_norm bits stay allocated. Source, clean bank and optional flag disjointness checks remain present.

The saved six-bit child phase mask remains in tower(child_norm) coordinates, and the matched return pays it against the reciprocal witness before that witness changes. The original record ownership checks remain.
The existing native fixture probes the intermediate inverse with arbitrary classical linear phase plus a cubic CCZ phase, so the recorded checks test more than an identity prefix/return composition.
The complete 4096-pair scalar test covers the one-bit norm toggle formula. Native pair tests sample 512 inputs under two fixed seeds; they are not an exhaustive 24-bit proof.
Local helper reduction does not establish whole-decoder width. Every remaining global peak and physical wire index must be accounted for before advertising Q888 or Q883.

borrowed_storage_contract.erase_restore_timing: after inverse_norm computed; before original_norm HMR; two consuming HMR loops in between

cost_formula: R * Q**2 * mean_T; compare on the same inputs and same repetition factor
limitations: The inverse return caller must supply inv0(prefix-entry) in the same source wires; Python ownership checks cannot inspect that quantum value.
The enclosing chart finite-output domain and its existing flag-reset contract are unchanged.
A new full-file hash can change the default official test cohort, so numerical score projections hold only under the explicitly stated same-input/same-R comparison.
